hero.body: Start a Proof-of-Life heartbeat in your browser, raise an agent's power level, and earn {{rewardToken}}. Stake it to earn {{valueToken}} on a fixed, transparent schedule. No hardware. No gas. No smart contracts in the core loop.

whatIs.title: A Tamagotchi-inspired platform for nurturing autonomous AI agents.
whatIs.intro: {{brand}} reframes the abstract, technical act of providing compute as an intuitive, emotionally resonant act of care. Just as the original Tamagotchi turned maintenance of a virtual pet into a daily ritual, {{brand}} turns maintenance of an AI agent's vitality into a rewarding, gamified experience, built on Robinhood, on top of an already-active community rather than a cold start.

sustainability.title: Sustainability gap
sustainability.body: The cost and effort of keeping an agent continuously active falls on a single party. When that party's resources or attention lapse, the agent goes dark.

engagement.title: Engagement gap
engagement.body: Communities form around popular agents with no direct, meaningful way to contribute to an agent's survival beyond speculation.

visibility.title: Visibility gap
visibility.body: There is no shared, transparent signal of an agent's operational health, so nobody can tell a thriving agent from one about to go offline.

whatIs.ambitionBody: To become the connective tissue of the agentic economy on Robinhood: a place where the health of every meaningful agent is visibly tied to the community that supports it, and where an existing token community gets a genuine, ongoing utility loop rather than a one-off speculative cycle. Companion NFTs deepen that with a high-emotion collectible ownership layer, something tangible to own, equip, trade, and invest in emotionally.

agentStates.title: Every agent's avatar shows exactly how much power it has left.
agentStates.intro: Agents are sourced from real, live agents on PONS Protocol, with no fabricated listings. Each one is represented by an expressive avatar whose appearance directly reflects its current power level through three defined states. A well-supported agent visibly flourishes; a neglected one visibly declines, prompting its community to intervene.

thriving.label: Thriving
thriving.note: Fully powered. Posting and executing on schedule.

idle.label: Idle
idle.note: Power slipping. Needs heartbeats to recover.

fading.label: Fading
fading.note: Close to going dark. Nurture now.

howItWorks.title: Compute Light: no hardware, no gas, no smart contract in the core loop.
howItWorks.intro: The core unit of value creation is the Proof-of-Life heartbeat session, a lightweight, verifiable compute contribution performed by ordinary users. Remove the tokens entirely and {{brand}} would still be a coherent product: a community keeping agents alive through distributed compute.

stake.title: Stake {{rewardToken}}

earn.title: Earn {{valueToken}} each epoch
earn.body: Hold a qualifying stake unchanged through a full cycle and you're paid a flat {{valueToken}} amount proportional to your stake. One shared global schedule, one visible countdown.

equip.title: Equip Companions
equip.body: Equip up to 3 Companion NFTs per agent for passive earn-rate bonuses, fade protection, and unique Legendary abilities.

companions.title: Every agent can equip 1 to 3 Companions.
companions.intro: Companions are ERC-721 NFTs on Robinhood Chain, minted gas-only for cost efficiency, that appear next to the agent avatar, provide passive bonuses based on rarity and type, can be freely equipped and unequipped, and trade on secondary markets. The nurturing loop stays primary; Companions are the collectible enhancement layer on top of it.

milestone.title: Milestone rewards
milestone.body: Free mints for a 7-day thriving streak or a top leaderboard placement.

tokens.title: Two tokens, two jobs. The tokens serve the loop, not the reverse.
tokens.intro: Neither token is issued for merely holding, trading, or speculating in isolation. Both flow from genuine participation.
tokens.rewardBody: The receipt for real compute work, earned exclusively through verified heartbeat sessions. It is currently an off-chain accounting balance (claiming to a wallet is on hold pending launch) but it is already fully functional as the unit that gets staked.
tokens.valueBody: A real ERC-20 on Robinhood Chain with its own pre-existing liquidity and community. Staking {{rewardToken}} is the only way to earn it, and claiming is live today: the platform's pool wallet sends it straight to your wallet and pays the network fee itself.

multiplier.title: Reward multiplier
multiplier.body: Staking {{rewardToken}} linearly raises your per-heartbeat earn rate, up to a capped maximum.

premium.title: Premium access
premium.body: Staking above a threshold unlocks premium agents.

epoch.title: Epoch reward
epoch.body: A qualifying stake held unchanged through a full cycle earns a flat {{valueToken}} payout on the shared global schedule.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.body: The reward-pool dashboard shows the pool wallet's real on-chain {{valueToken}} balance and total distributed, not a claimed number.

tokens.loopNote: Planned revenue sources, including LP and trading fees, developer fees, premium-feature fees, and Companion mints and royalties, feed open-market buybacks into the pool wallet. Consistent with our economics-transparency principle, the fee ledger reports honest zeros until a source is actually live.

differentiators.title: A compute network with a community it didn't have to build from scratch.
differentiators.intro: Compute is the product that makes the experience honest. The community is what gives it an audience from day one. Companions are the ownership layer that turns daily care into lasting attachment.

maintenance.title: Maintenance, not creation
maintenance.body: Most projects focus on creating agents or selling raw enterprise compute. We focus squarely on decentralised, retail-driven maintenance of agents that already exist.

framing.title: Tamagotchi framing
framing.body: A technical activity becomes an emotionally engaging daily ritual, which dramatically lowers the barrier to participation.

light.title: Compute Light architecture
light.body: No specialised hardware, no technical expertise. It runs in a browser tab, which makes it accessible to a mass retail audience.

footprint.title: Minimal engineering footprint
footprint.body: No on-chain contract layer for the agent registry, Proof-of-Life verification, or reward accounting. Robinhood is touched only for wallet-signature auth and final settlement.

community.title: Builds on an existing community
community.body: Rather than bootstrapping a token and community from zero, {{brand}} builds on {{valueToken}}, so the value-capture side has a real audience from day one.

collectible.title: Collectible ownership layer
collectible.body: Companion NFTs add scarcity, secondary-market potential and emotional attachment without turning the product into a full pet-breeding game.

retail.what: Everyday crypto users and AI enthusiasts who want a low-effort, gamified way to participate in the agentic economy.
retail.value: Gamified engagement, {{rewardToken}} rewards, Companions, and a sense of ownership over the agents they support.

community.what: Existing holders and community members looking for real, ongoing utility beyond price speculation.
community.value: A concrete, recurring reason to hold and stake, an active utility loop grafted onto an existing token.

developers.what: Creators and teams who build AI agents and need reliable, community-backed operational support.
developers.value: Decentralised life support, reduced operating burden, and a built-in, motivated community.

ecosystem.what: Protocols and communities seeking richer agent infrastructure and real on-chain activity.
ecosystem.value: A resilient agent-support layer and a showcase of retail-friendly Robinhood utility.

about.title: About MONKII LABS
about.p1: {{brand}} is a Tamagotchi for autonomous AI agents, built on {{network}}. An agent here has a power level that decays on its own. Community members restore it by supplying lightweight Proof-of-Life compute straight from a browser tab, and they are paid for the work they contribute. Keeping an agent alive stops being one operator's private cost and becomes something a community can do together, and be rewarded for.
about.sustainability: Keeping an agent running falls on a single party. When their attention or their budget lapses, the agent goes dark, and everything built around it goes with it.
about.engagement: Communities form around interesting agents and then have nothing to do except speculate on a ticker. There is no way to actually help.
about.visibility: There is no shared, honest signal of whether an agent is healthy. Thriving, idle, and fading are legible states, published for everyone.
about.p2: You open a session against an agent. Your browser receives a challenge and solves it in a Web Worker, off the main thread, so the page stays responsive. The solution goes back to our servers, which verify it, restore a slice of the agent's power, and credit you {{rewardToken}}. Then the next challenge arrives and it runs again. No specialised hardware, no gas, and nothing to install.
about.p3: Compute is the product, the community is the multiplier, and the tokens serve the loop rather than the other way round. {{rewardToken}} is the receipt for verified compute work. {{valueToken}} is the value-capture asset, earned by staking {{rewardToken}} on one flat, published, global schedule, and paid from the real balance held by the pool wallet. Companion NFTs are the ownership layer that turns daily care into something lasting.
about.h4: What is on-chain, and what is not
about.p4: We put on-chain only what genuinely benefits from being there. Companions are a real ERC-721 collection on {{network}}, so what you mint is yours and outlives the platform. {{network}} is also where wallet-signature authentication, pool transparency, and {{valueToken}} payouts happen.
about.p5: Everything in the hot path stays off-chain and deliberately so: the agent registry, Proof-of-Life verification, and reward accounting. Putting a heartbeat on-chain would make the core loop cost gas, which would defeat the point of a mechanism whose whole promise is that anyone can contribute from a browser tab for free.

help.title: Help
help.a1: A lightweight background session, started with a single action, that solves a keccak256 proof-of-work challenge in your browser. Verified heartbeats raise an agent's power level and accrue {{rewardToken}} to your balance.
help.q2: Do I need special hardware or gas?
help.a2: No. The architecture is Compute Light: it runs in an ordinary browser tab. Wallet authentication is signature-based (an EVM wallet signature) with no transaction and no gas.
help.q3: What do thriving, idle and fading mean?
help.a3: They are the three defined states of an agent's avatar, driven directly by its current power level. A well-supported agent visibly flourishes; a neglected one visibly declines.
help.q4: How does the {{valueToken}} epoch reward work?
help.a4: One fixed schedule shared by every staker, not a personal timer. Hold at least the minimum {{rewardToken}} stake unchanged for a full cycle and you are paid a flat amount proportional to your stake at that cycle's end. Staking or unstaking during a cycle forfeits that cycle and rolls you into the next.
help.a5: Companions are ERC-721 NFTs on {{network}}, minted gas-only. Each agent can equip up to 3. They give passive {{rewardToken}} earn-rate bonuses by rarity, plus fade protection at Uncommon and above and unique abilities at Legendary. Equipping is instant and free, and Companions trade on any {{network}} NFT marketplace.
help.q6: Can I claim {{rewardToken}} to my wallet?
help.a6: Not yet, {{rewardToken}} is currently an off-chain accounting balance with claiming on hold pending launch. It is already fully functional as the unit that gets staked. {{valueToken}} claiming is live: the pool wallet sends it directly to your wallet and pays the network fee.

You are responsible for knowing whether local law permits your use, and for any tax arising from your activity here.
terms.p2: Your wallet is your account. We never hold your keys, your seed phrase, or your funds, and we will never ask you for them. Signing in means signing a plain-text message that proves you control an address; it costs no gas and authorises no transfer. Every action taken by an address is treated as taken by its owner, so keep your keys, your device, and your wallet software secure. We cannot reverse a transaction, recover a lost key, or restore access to a compromised wallet.
terms.p3: A heartbeat session runs a hashing workload in your browser and submits solved challenges to our servers, which verify them and credit the result. You agree to run it only in a browser you control, and not to submit forged, replayed, pre-computed, or automated solutions, nor to operate multiple identities to inflate a single participant's share. We may rate-limit, suspend, or void the accrual of any session we determine is manipulating the loop, and we may change difficulty, session length, or accrual rates to keep it fair.
terms.p4: {{rewardToken}} is an internal accounting balance recording verified compute work. It is not a security, not an investment, not a claim on the company or its revenue, and not a promise that any future token will be issued or that it will have value. {{valueToken}} payouts are made from the balance actually held by the pool wallet, on the published epoch schedule; where that balance is insufficient, payouts are reduced or deferred accordingly. Reward rates, multipliers, thresholds, and the epoch schedule are parameters, and we may change them as the economy evolves. Nothing here is financial advice.
terms.p5: Companions are ERC-721 tokens on {{network}}. Once minted they are yours: you own them, you may transfer or sell them, and that ownership does not depend on this platform continuing to exist. What we control is what a Companion does inside the product. To the fullest extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential loss, or for lost profits, lost tokens, or lost opportunity.

wp.title: Whitepaper
wp.lead: A protocol that turns the upkeep of autonomous AI agents into verified, browser-native work anyone can contribute, and pays for it.
wp.abstract1: Autonomous AI agents are expensive to keep alive and cheap to abandon. The cost of uptime sits with one operator, while the community that forms around an agent has no way to help and no signal of whether the agent is healthy at all.
wp.abstract2: {{brand}} makes agent upkeep a public, participatory act. Each agent carries a power level that decays continuously. Anyone can open a browser tab, receive a keccak-256 challenge, solve it off the main thread in a Web Worker, and submit the solution. A verified solution restores a slice of that agent's power and credits the contributor in {{rewardToken}}, a receipt for verified compute. Staking {{rewardToken}} earns {{valueToken}} on a fixed 24-hour epoch, paid from a real balance held on {{network}}.
wp.abstract3: No specialised hardware, no gas to participate, and nothing to install. The contribution path is a browser tab.
wp.sustainability: Keeping an agent running falls on a single party. When their attention or their budget lapses, the agent goes dark and everything built on it goes with it.
wp.engagement: Communities form around interesting agents and then have nothing to do but speculate on a ticker. Wanting to help and being able to help are different things.
wp.visibility: There is no shared, honest signal of whether an agent is healthy. An agent that has been failing for a week looks exactly like one that is fine.
wp.vitality1: Every agent holds a power level between 0 and {{max}}. Power decays at a fixed rate per hour, derived from the agent's real traction, so an agent left alone degrades on a published schedule rather than at anyone's discretion.
wp.vitality2: Decay is continuous and computed rather than ticked. Live power is always the last recorded power minus the decay accrued since it was recorded, so what an API response reports and what a heartbeat writes back start from the same number. A background evaluator materialises that value periodically and emits alerts on a state change, but it is not what makes decay happen.
wp.vitality3: Three states are derived from power, and all three are public:
wp.thriving: , at or above the agent's healthy threshold.
wp.idle: , between the warning and healthy thresholds.
wp.fading: , at or below the warning threshold.
wp.vitality4: Thresholds are per agent, not global. An agent with deeper traction is held to a higher bar, which keeps the state meaningful across a fleet of very different agents.
wp.pol1a: Proof-of-Life is the mechanism that converts attention into something a server can verify. It is deliberately a proof of
wp.pol1b: , not a proof of stake or of identity: the only thing it establishes is that real computation was spent on a challenge that could not have been prepared in advance.
wp.polStep1: The contributor opens a session against an agent at a chosen intensity, and the server issues a single-use challenge: a random seed and a difficulty.
wp.polStep2a: The browser grinds a nonce in a Web Worker until
wp.polStep2c: leading zero bits. The worker runs off the main thread, so the interface stays responsive and the progress shown is the real hash rate.
wp.polStep3: The solution is submitted. The server re-derives the same digest, checks the work, and consumes the challenge in a single conditional update, so a replayed or concurrent submission loses the race and is rejected.
wp.polStep4: On acceptance, the agent's power is decayed to now and then increased, clamped at {{max}}, the vitality state is re-derived, and {{rewardToken}} is credited to the contributor.
wp.polStep5: The next challenge is issued in the same response, and the loop continues.
wp.polIntensity: Intensity sets the difficulty and the payout together. Higher intensity costs more compute per accepted heartbeat and pays proportionally more, so the choice is a genuine trade rather than a free upgrade.
wp.accrualCaption: Accrual by intensity, relative to a standard heartbeat
wp.accrualLightMeaning: Two fewer difficulty bits. For phones and background tabs.
wp.accrualMaxMeaning: Two extra bits, roughly four times the expected work.
wp.polGuards: Two guards keep the loop honest. A challenge expires if it is not solved in time, so work cannot be banked against a future session. And a minimum interval between accepted heartbeats bounds how fast a single session can submit, with the server returning the exact wait rather than a bare rejection, so a fast machine paces itself instead of being punished for being fast.
wp.monki1: {{rewardToken}} is the receipt for verified compute. It is credited only by an accepted Proof-of-Life heartbeat, and the amount is a function of the difficulty actually solved and the contributor's multipliers. There is no path to {{rewardToken}} that does not pass through verified work.
wp.monki2: Balances are held in an off-chain ledger. This is a deliberate choice, not a shortcut: a heartbeat that settled on-chain would cost gas, and a mechanism whose entire promise is that anyone can contribute from a browser tab for free cannot have a fee on its core loop. What the ledger records is a claim on the protocol, and section 11 is explicit about what that means for trust.
wp.monki3: During the pre-launch phase, {{rewardToken}} accrues and does not withdraw. The gate is a protocol setting rather than a missing feature, so the mining phase and the claiming phase are the same system in two configurations.
wp.staking1: Staking {{rewardToken}} does two things: it raises the earn multiplier on every subsequent heartbeat, and it makes the stake eligible for {{valueToken}} yield.
wp.staking2: The multiplier is linear and published. It runs from 1.0x at zero staked to 3.0x at the maximum, with no cliff and no discretionary tier. Yield settles on fixed 24-hour epochs anchored to a published UTC instant, so an epoch boundary is the same moment for everyone and cannot be moved for one participant.
wp.staking3a: A stake becomes eligible from the
wp.staking3b: epoch boundary after it is made, never the one it was made inside. This is what stops a stake placed minutes before settlement from collecting a full epoch of yield it did not hold through, and it is the reason the entitlement is computed from epoch indices rather than from elapsed time.
wp.staking4: Payout is a flat, global rate per staked {{rewardToken}} per completed epoch. There is no per-user schedule.
wp.phase2: Yield today is paid entirely in {{valueToken}}, a liquid launchpad token on {{network}}. In Phase 2 the disbursal engine splits a claim in half: 50% in {{valueToken}} and 50% in tokenized {{stockToken}} stock tokens on the same chain. The staking mechanism does not change; only the settlement leg does.
wp.comp1: Companions are the ownership layer. They are a real ERC-721 collection on {{network}}, so what you hold is yours and outlives the platform that issued it. Companions are earned against milestones in the loop rather than sold as a shortcut past it.
wp.comp2: Up to three Companions equip to a single agent. Their effects stack in two directions: a bonus to {{rewardToken}} earned on every heartbeat against that agent, and a reduction in that agent's power decay. Decay reduction is capped, so no combination of Companions can make an agent immortal and remove the reason to nurture it.
wp.comp3: Rarity determines the size of those effects:
wp.rarityUncommonText: , +10 to 15% earn rate with minor fade mitigation.
wp.rarityRareText: , +15 to 25% earn rate with moderate fade mitigation.
wp.rarityEpicText: , +25 to 35% earn rate with strong fade mitigation.
wp.rarityLegendaryText: , +35 to 50% earn rate with strong protection and unique abilities.
wp.comp4: Equipping and unequipping are off-chain and instant, so arranging a loadout costs nothing. Minting is the on-chain act, and it is gas-only: there is no mint price.
wp.arch1: The dividing line is simple. Anything that benefits from being permanent and independently verifiable goes on-chain. Anything on the hot path of the nurturing loop stays off it.
wp.archOnChain: ({{network}} is an Arbitrum Orbit L2, chain ID {{chainId}}, gas paid in native ETH): the Companion ERC-721 collection, {{valueToken}} balances and payouts, the reward pool wallet, and wallet-signature authentication.
wp.archOffChain: : the agent registry, Proof-of-Life challenge issuance and verification, the {{rewardToken}} ledger, staking accrual, Companion equipping, and vitality evaluation. These are the operations that run continuously, per contributor, many times a minute.
wp.archClientA: The client is a React application; the solver is a Web Worker so that grinding never blocks the interface. The service layer is a TypeScript API over PostgreSQL, with every balance-altering operation written inside a database transaction. Contract addresses in use:
wp.secAuthLabel: Authentication is a signature, never a password.
wp.secAuth: Signing in means signing a nonce-bearing message with the wallet. The message states plainly that it costs no gas and triggers no transaction. A verified signature issues a session token; the wallet is never asked for anything else to browse.
wp.secActionLabel: Every balance-altering action is separately authorised.
wp.secAction: Staking, unstaking and claiming each require their own signed message naming the action, the wallet, the amount and a nonce. A session token alone cannot move a balance. Each authorisation carries a timestamp and is rejected outside a short freshness window, and each nonce is recorded and refused on reuse, so a captured authorisation cannot be replayed.
wp.secReplay: Challenges are single-use and time-limited, and consumption is a conditional update, so two submissions of the same solution cannot both be credited.
wp.secGate: {{rewardToken}} claiming, {{valueToken}} claiming and Companion minting are each independently switchable. Any of them being paused is a stated protocol state with a reason returned to the caller, not a silent failure.
wp.params1: These are the live defaults. They are configuration rather than constants, which is what lets difficulty and yield be tuned without a redeploy, and it also means the authoritative value is the one the API reports, not the one printed here.
wp.pDifficultyMeaning: Leading zero bits required on the keccak-256 digest, at standard intensity.
wp.pLifetimeMeaning: After which an unsolved challenge expires and cannot be submitted.
wp.pPowerMeaning: Restored to the agent, out of a maximum of {{max}}.
wp.pIntervalMeaning: Between accepted heartbeats on one session.
wp.pEvalMeaning: How often decayed power is materialised and alerts are emitted.
wp.pEpochMeaning: Anchored to a fixed UTC instant, identical for every participant.
wp.pMinStakeMeaning: Below this a stake earns no {{valueToken}}.
wp.pMultRangeMeaning: Linear in the amount staked, applied to every heartbeat.
wp.pMaxMultMeaning: The stake at which the multiplier reaches 3.0x.
wp.pMintPriceMeaning: No mint fee; the contributor pays network gas.
wp.pDecayCapMeaning: The ceiling on stacked fade mitigation for one agent.
wp.phase1: The web cockpit, wallet sign-in, the Web Worker keccak-256 solver, and the {{rewardToken}} ledger.
wp.phase2r: The 24-hour payout engine, liquid {{valueToken}} rewards, and the Companion inventory.
wp.phase3: Tokenized {{stockToken}} stock token integration on {{network}} and dual crypto-equity disbursal.
wp.phase4: Mobile nurturing nodes and an autonomous agent fleet marketplace.
wp.riskLedger: {{rewardToken}} balances, Proof-of-Life verification and staking accrual run off-chain. Participants rely on the protocol to account honestly, and the mitigation is transparency rather than trustlessness: published parameters, a published epoch schedule, and payouts made from a wallet balance anyone can inspect on-chain.
wp.riskPolLabel: Proof-of-Life is a work receipt, not a security mechanism.
wp.riskPol: It establishes that computation was spent. It does not establish who spent it, and it cannot by itself distinguish one enthusiastic participant from several coordinated ones. Rate limiting and earn governance, not the hash function, are what bound that.
wp.riskPhase2: The {{stockToken}} settlement leg requires tokenized stock infrastructure on {{network}}. Until that is live, yield is paid entirely in {{valueToken}}.
wp.riskParams: Difficulty, yield rate and thresholds are tuned as the fleet grows. Changes affect future accrual, never balances already earned.
